content.text:
Diagnosis while CI runs:

**The lint failures weren't from the merge** — they were a repo-wide time bomb that went off between 2026-07-28 (last green Lint on `main`) and now.

`lint.yml` used `go-version: "stable"` for setup-go, while the repo pins its toolchain in `mise.toml`:

```
go = "1.26.0"
golangci-lint = "2.11.3"
```

When `stable` floated to Go 1.27.0, golangci-lint v2.11.3 (built with go1.26.1) could no longer decode the 1.27 stdlib's export data:

```
could not import encoding/json (... cannot decode "cmp",
export data version 4 is greater than maximum supported version 2)
```

Every module fails identically at typecheck, which is why all seven `lint-agents` jobs plus `lint-e2e` went red while `test-agents` stayed green — CI's test jobs use `mise-action`, so they got the pinned Go 1.26.0. Only `lint.yml` diverged.

**Fix:** `go-version-file` pointing at each module's own `go.mod`, so setup-go reads the declared `go 1.26.0` instead of floating. No duplicated version literal, and it tracks `go.mod` automatically.

I considered bumping golangci-lint to v2.13.2 instead (v2.13.0 added `go1.27 support`). I downloaded it and ran it locally first — it trades one breakage for another, surfacing new `goconst` findings in goose, grok, and omp. That's a real upgrade worth doing, but it means touching two agents this PR has nothing to do with, so it belongs in its own PR.

**Verified locally before pushing**, with the actual pinned v2.11.3 binary on Go 1.26:

| Module | Result |
|---|---|
| amp, goose, grok, kilo, kiro, omp, qwen, e2e | all clean |

`gofmt -l .` clean, `lint.yml` valid YAML. Pushed as `2ff2609`.

One caveat worth flagging: this is a repo-wide CI fix riding in a Grok PR, and `main` is red for the same reason. You may want it cherry-picked to `main` directly rather than waiting on #64 to merge.

I'll report the CI results when the run finishes.
